lines.text: Three animals that sleep in the craziest ways.
First, sea otters. If one falls asleep alone, the current can carry it far out to sea.
So they hold hands while they sleep, so nobody drifts away.
Some even wrap themselves in kelp, like a blanket tied to the ocean floor.
And the babies? They just nap on mom's belly.
Next, the frigatebird. It can stay in the air for two whole months without landing.
So it sleeps while flying, in naps that last about twelve seconds,
often with half of its brain still awake to watch where it's going.
Add it all up, and that's less than forty-five minutes of sleep a day.
Finally, sperm whales. They sleep standing straight up, hanging just below the surface like giant tree trunks.
The whole group goes completely still for up to fifteen minutes.
When scientists drifted their boat right into a sleeping pod, the whales didn't even notice.
Until the boat bumped one, and the whole group woke up at once.
